title: The 1982 radiation pulse masks part of the SST feedback gap in nine controlled model pairs
abstract: We tested a short radiation pulse in nine published atmosphere-model pairs that differ only in SST forcing. In 1982, AMIP-minus-HadISST1 net downward radiation is 0.511 W m-2 below the mean of 1981 and 1983. All nine contrasts are negative. The mean exceeds all 108 earlier absolute annual contrasts. Shortwave cloud radiative effect supplies 64% of the pulse. Excluding 1982 from both experiments makes the mean 1981-2010 regression feedback gap more negative, from -0.243 to -0.382 W m-2 K-1. This change has the same sign in all nine pairs. Thus the short pulse masks part of the later slope gap. Separate pulse-and-step fits retain a large short pulse but give a window-dependent lasting step. These are sample sensitivity results, not an SST correction. Year-block bootstrap limits include zero. Annual global data cannot prove that the November 1981 SST source switch caused the pulse or identify which SST product is correct. We supply code, hashes, fit tables and resampling draws.
